relations.subject: tool:couchbase-cli-cluster-init
relations.evidence: Specifies what IP family the cluster should used. The default option is 'ipv4'. When 'ipv4-only' or 'ipv6-only' is used the cluster will only listen on that address.

relations.subject: tool:couchbase-cli-cluster-init
relations.evidence: Specifies if node to node encryption should be used. The default option is 'off'. When set to 'on' all communications between nodes will be over a encrypted connection.

notable_absence.finding: cluster-init.md never mentions RBAC at all, which is actually expected and correct here (this is the bootstrap command that creates the very first administrator account, before any role model exists to check against) - unlike cluster-edit.md and server-add.md, whose absence of a role requirement is notable precisely because roles DO already exist by the time those commands run. Flagging the contrast: this is the one page in the batch where the absence is structurally justified rather than a review gap.

cross_component_finding: The --services option's accepted value 'fts' and the --cluster-fts-ramsize flag both use the CLI's legacy 'full-text service' framing ('Sets the full-text service memory quota (in MiB)... if the full-text service is specified in the --services option') where the rest of the corpus's promoted vocabulary has moved to service:search-service ('Search service'). This is consistent CLI-wide terminology lag rather than a one-off: the same 'fts'/'full-text' framing recurs verbatim on cluster-edit.md in this same batch. Separately, --update-notifications' option description embeds a full paragraph of privacy-policy prose (what data is collected, browser/geolocation info, a pointer to the 'Couchbase Server Privacy FAQ') directly inside a single CLI flag's description rather than linking out to a dedicated page - an unusual density of legal/product text for a terse reference-page format, consistent with lighter editorial pass-through from source rather than TW restructuring.
cross_product_finding: Plainly none - the page documents self-managed Server cluster bootstrap (service placement, memory quotas, IP family, node-to-node encryption) with no Capella equivalent stated or implied; Capella provisions clusters through its own management plane, not this CLI.
